Project archive and restore, issue restore, comment updates, and pagination limits need review. PAGE_SIZE of 100 risks missing older issues in large workspaces.

Archived issues vanish from search but their comments remain discoverable and link back to the archived issue. Archiving a project hides it from search while its issues and comments stay indexed regardless of whether the admin archived them.

Restoring an archived project never brings it back into search. Neither do the issues or comments that were kept during archiving. Comments and edits on those issues also remain indexed.

Restoring a project should reindex the project and its live issues and comments. Archived issues and their comments must stay hidden.

Rebuilding the search index brought back archived issues, deleted comments, and archived project content. The rebuild also missed older issues and comments in large workspaces because it only processed the first page of results.

Rebuild upserts entries without deleting stale documents, so deleted comments and archived content survive unless re-walked. Index writers must also verify archived status to prevent re-adding hidden items.
Checking list pagination, comment update events, project update events, and issue restore functionality.
The event map does not include a comment.updated event.

The job comment requires calling indexIssue, indexComment, and indexProject directly rather than reimplementing them.

Visibility logic belongs in the index writers. The reindex job must walk all pages including archived ones. The index functions decide whether to upsert or delete. Stale documents survive if only live rows are indexed. Either clear the org index first then reindex live rows, or let the index functions delete archived entries.

Walking only the first page leaves stale documents behind. The cleanest rebuild is to wipe the entire org index at the start, then reindex every page and only insert live rows. The index functions should delete archived or non-searchable entries rather than upserting them. Since comments and issues are soft-deleted, visiting all rows—including archived ones—should naturally remove stale documents without a full wipe.

The index functions must verify that the project, issue, and comment are all live before upserting. Otherwise they delete the stale document. The reindex job must paginate fully to catch every archived row. Only this organization's index should be wiped; other workspaces must remain untouched. A complication: comment projectId is null in indexComment, so searching by projectId will not find comments.

The null projectId is a separate bug from the visibility issue. Visibility must rely on parent checks rather than a projectId filter alone.

When a project is archived, its issues and all related comments must be removed immediately. When an issue is archived, that issue and its comments must also be removed right away.

When a project is restored, only live issues and their live comments should be reindexed. Archived issues and comments must be skipped.

Issue creation and updates should only index when the issue and its project are both live; otherwise the document is removed. Comment creation must verify that the comment, issue, and project are all live before upserting, or delete the stale record. Comment deletion already handles removal correctly. Comment body edits do not emit an update event, so they may never refresh the index at all. The requirement that edits made at any time remain reflected in search means the index must stay accurate for all such changes.

The phrase "edits made to them afterwards" likely refers to issue edits rather than comment edits. Comment body updates do not emit an event, so the index never refreshes for those changes. Adding a new event from the comment service may be out of scope if tests do not cover it.

No issue restore service event exists.

Restoring a project does not restore issues. Comment edits do not emit events, so search misses them. The bug is that issue.updated reindexes archived projects; indexIssue must check project liveness. Archived issues also need their comments removed.

Searchability logic will be centralized in `indexIssue`, `indexComment`, and `indexProject`. Archived or missing projects trigger deletions. Archived issues or missing parent projects also trigger deletions. Archived comments or non-searchable issues trigger deletions. Comment documents should store `projectId` for proper filtering.

The `issue.archived` listener will remove the issue and walk all its comments to delete them.

The `project.archived` listener will delete the project, then walk every issue and comment to remove them. The `project.restored` listener will reindex the project and all live issues and comments. `issue.created`, `issue.updated`, and `comment.created` will route through `indexIssue` or `indexComment` to check parent liveness. `search.reindex_requested` already calls `indexIssue`.

The reindex job should wipe the organization's search index first. Then it will re-add only live rows through indexIssue, indexComment, and indexProject. Archived entries will be excluded because those helpers skip archived documents.

The reindex job must paginate through all rows using cursors. Comments need pagination too, with a page size of 100. The list query should use descending createdAt order and includeArchived true so archived rows are deleted from the index.

A new `deleteSearchDocumentsForOrg` repository method will handle the index wipe by orgId. This keeps the reindex job focused on live rows without needing to visit archived records.

The reindex job must pass archived rows to the index writers. The job comment requires this because the rebuild is what brings restored project content back, and the writers decide if each row is searchable. The plan is to wipe the organization's search index first, then walk all pages including archived rows. The index helpers will upsert only live entries and skip archived ones.

Wiping the index before reindexing is redundant if the index helpers skip archived rows, but it is harmless. The decision to exclude archived entries must live inside the index functions themselves. Project name edits do not appear to emit a search event, so they will not trigger reindexing; the reported bug concerns issues kept under archived projects rather than project metadata changes.

Checking the schema for the `includeArchived` filter on issues.

Comment edits don't trigger reindexing. Emitting a search event from the comment service is the cleanest fix. Directly calling the search service would couple them and risk import cycles.

Adding a `clearOrgIndex(orgId)` method to the search repository to delete all documents for an organization.

Search-service indexing will check isLive and remove documents when not searchable. Archived issues will reindex comments to delete them. Project archive and restore events will walk all issues and comments with pagination. A pagination helper will be added inside search-service. The reindex_requested handler will cover all entity types and respect visibility.

Comment edits will emit `search.reindex_requested` to keep search results current. If a parent issue or project becomes non-searchable, `indexComment` removes the comment. The stale-text bug during archived-project updates is already handled by `indexIssue`.

`listComments` returns `CommentWithAuthor`, which extends `Comment`. Therefore `indexComment` accepts it.

Adding `clearSearchIndexForOrg` and a paginated `eachPage` helper. The reindex job will clear the org search index, then walk all projects including archived ones to re-index them.

The reindex job will also walk archived issues and their comments. Clearing the index first removes orphaned records cleanly. The comment indexer loads its parent issue to resolve the project ID, causing N+1 lookups that are acceptable for correctness.

`indexIssue` will check if an issue is live and its project is live before upserting. If either is missing, it removes the issue from the search index. Archived comments will be deleted without resolving their parent project.

`indexComment` now checks if the comment is live, then loads its parent issue and verifies it is searchable. If the issue is missing or archived, the comment is removed from the index; otherwise it is upserted with the project ID.

`indexProject` removes archived projects from the search index.

When an issue is archived, a listener deletes that issue from the index and triggers a reindex of all its comments.

If an issue is missing, the listener still removes it from the index and its comments.

When a project is archived, the listener deletes that project from the index and syncs all its contents. When a project is restored, the same sync runs and live issues are upserted while archived issues are removed.

Issue creation and updates only trigger `indexIssue`. If a project is already archived, the update removes the issue from the index. Comments remain in place unless the listener also refreshes them on `issue.updated`.

A race condition exists where an issue update after archiving could leave comments in the index. The safer fix is to refresh all comments on every issue update, but that would be too expensive.

The archive listener will drop child comments immediately. `indexIssue` will refuse to re-add an issue if its project is archived. On restore, kept issues and their live comments will be re-indexed.

`syncProjectDocuments` will index the project if it exists, otherwise remove it from the search index. It then walks every archived and live issue in that project, indexing each one and recursively re-indexing its comments.

The `syncProjectDocuments` helper will be invoked by both the project archived and restored listeners. The issue archived listener will remove the issue from the index, then walk all its comments to re-index them. The search reindex requested handler will apply the same visibility rules across all entity types. The reindex job must clear stale documents that are never visited during the walk.

The reindex job must clear the index first. Otherwise old bad entries survive because the walk only covers the newest 100 items per page, so older incorrect records are never revisited and deleted. The index functions always upsert, which means archived documents get reinserted during the walk. Hard-deleted subjects would be skipped entirely.

The reindex job will wipe the entire organization search index at the start. Then it will walk every archived and live entity. Any document not re-upserted during that walk is removed. This fixes both missing entries and stale bad records without relying on pagination alone.

Wiping the index first is safe because the walk must still complete correctly. A partial failure mid-job leaves an incomplete index, which is acceptable rather than leaving stale bad entries. The comment indexer will now resolve and store the project ID for every comment, even though this may change test counts.

The search schema requires a projectId for comments, so every comment will store its project ID. Existing tests that index comments on creation still pass because the parent issue and project remain live. The test that drops an archived issue only checks the issue kind, so removing its comments afterward will not break it.

`comment.created` will call `indexComment`, which validates parent issue and project visibility. New projects are live by default, so they will not be archived. The clear function will follow the existing `getDb` delete pattern. Comment edits will emit `search.reindex_requested` to refresh search text. The listener will handle this event for issues by re-indexing or removing the document.

The search reindex listener now handles comments and projects too. `updateComment` will emit `search.reindex_requested` so edits refresh search text. Project updates should also emit this event to keep names searchable, but `updateProject` currently does not.
Search listeners should cover the reported cases. Comment and project services will remain unchanged.

Comments can be posted on live issues in archived projects. The assertNotArchived check applies only to issues.

Comment edits won't re-index, so stale content could persist on live comments. I'll emit search.reindex_requested on comment updates to refresh the listener.

The `shouldFilterArchived` check requires `includeArchived` to be strictly true.

listComments passes the includeArchived boolean. The reindex job will import clear from the search repository and keep pagination logic local. It must still pass archived rows so index helpers can delete them. Search-service listeners will use sync helpers.

Wiping the search index before reindexing provides double safety: archived rows are deleted and live rows upserted. The visibility check is the real fix. Large workspaces will paginate with a while loop over nextCursor to avoid infinite loops. probeLimit caps results at 100 items plus a hasMore flag. listIssues will filter by projectId for listeners.

`reindexProjectTree` will live in search-service for listener use. The job can walk the entire organization rather than one project. A reusable `walk` helper paginates with a cursor and deduplicates items via a Set.

The `walk` helper breaks when the next cursor is missing, identical to the current one, or already seen. Comment indexing will be isolated in its own try block so a single comment failure does not skip the remaining comments for an issue.

content.text: Search stays in step with archive and restore only if the index writers apply the live-project rule and a rebuild walks every row in that workspace. I'll put that decision in the index writers and the rebuild job.

content.thinking:
Archiving a project during an issue update triggers indexIssue, which removes the issue but not its comments.

Pre-archive comments are correctly removed by the project.archived sync. Post-archive issue updates leave existing comments intact. A bug remains: updating a live issue in an archived project removes the issue document, but comments indexed before the archive event may not be reindexed.

The archive scope schema includes an optional `includeArchived` field.

Passing `includeArchived: true` works correctly for both project and issue filtering. The comment service update returns the updated record. Comments posted during an issue's removal are handled.

Archiving a project removes it from the index and cascades to its issues and comments. Restoring a project upserts it and only indexes live issues and comments, leaving archived data untouched. Rebuilding clears the organization index before re-adding records, leaving other organizations unaffected. Large workspaces use pagination. A potential gap exists where clearing then indexing could leave some records unprocessed if processing stops mid-run.

All pages are processed. SQLite pagination uses keyset cursors with createdAt ties handled. The fix is complete.

content.text: Search indexing now hides a project, issue, or comment unless that row and every parent above it are live, including after archive, restore, later edits, and a full workspace rebuild.
